newsitem.title: USA: Repeal of utility holding company law dead for now.
newsitem.headline: Repeal of utility holding company law dead for now.

text.p: Congressional efforts to repeal the 60-year-old Public Utility Holding Company Act are dead for this year, with Congress focused on passing spending bills before adjourning, industry officials said Wednesday.

But a coalition of companies seeking repeal of the law, which was designed to protect ratepayers from subsidizing electric utility holding companies' unprofitable attempts to diversify into unrelated businesses, said it planned to push the bill next year.
"We think that the progress we've made this past year really lays the foundation for us to proceed in the next Congress," said John Howes, spokesman for the Repeal PUHCA Now coalition.
The Senate banking committee passed a bill in June to repeal the law.

The coalition, which includes utilities that support and oppose efforts to open the whole power market to competition, said it would continue to pursue repeal of the law separately from comprehensive electricity reform bills.
PUHCA repeal "has its own movement now," Howes said.
